title: World War I: Causes and Consequences
text: World War I (1914–1918) was a global conflict that began in Europe and involved most of the world's great powers. It was triggered by the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand of Austria-Hungary in Sarajevo on June 28, 1914, which set off a chain of alliances and mobilizations. The war introduced mechanized warfare on a massive scale, including trench warfare, poison gas, tanks, and aerial combat. Approximately 20 million people died, including both military personnel and civilians. The war ended with the Treaty of Versailles in 1919, which imposed harsh conditions on Germany, contributing to economic instability and resentment that would eventually lead to World War II.
